# Faber — full agent reference

Expanded machine map for agents working on Faber language packages.
Start with https://faberlang.dev/llms.txt if you have not already.

Host: https://faberlang.dev
Current CLI release: Faber 1.5.0 (tag faber-v1.5.0)

## Site URL rules (read this)

- `/` is the **product landing page** (compute-first homepage).
- `/porta/` is the **locale chooser** (language portal).
- Authored HTML documentation lives under **`/en-US/…`** (English is the full prose authority).
- Other site locales (`/th-TH/`, `/zh-Hans/`, `/zh-Hant/`, `/vi/`, `/ar/`, `/hi/`)
  ship reader packs + corpus; authored prose may still fall back to English.
  Prefer `/en-US/` unless the user asked otherwise.
- Bare paths such as `/start/install.html` are **redirect stubs** to `/en-US/…`.
  Cite the `/en-US/…` form in agent-facing docs and skills.

## Identity

- Language name: Faber (Latin "maker" / craftsman)
- Compiler name: Radix (Latin "root") — implementation private; ships inside `faber` CLI
- License: MIT
- Designer: Ian Zepp
- First appeared: 2025

## Architectural invariant

Meaning lives in HIR (high-level intermediate representation). Reader locales
(Latin, Thai, Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Vietnamese, …) and codegen targets
(Rust, and others) are renderings of the same semantic core. Do not treat
any single surface syntax as the only authority.

## Type and glyph system (agent checklist)

1. Declarations are type-first: `textus nomen`, `numerus x`, `bivalens ok`.
2. Functions: `functio name(type param, …) → return_type { … }`.
3. Bind: `←`. Equality: `≡`. Compact branch: `si cond ergo body`.
4. Nullable: `T ∪ nihil`. Prefer explicit union over inventing `?` sugar.
5. Return: `redde expr`.
6. Comments: only `#` on its own line. LEX006/LEX007 if you use `//` or trailing `#`.
7. Packages need `faber.toml` and sources under `src/`.

## Install assets (1.5.0)

Release: https://github.com/faberlang/releases/releases/tag/faber-v1.5.0

| Platform | URL |
|---|---|
| macOS arm64 tar.gz | https://github.com/faberlang/releases/releases/download/faber-v1.5.0/faber-v1.5.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz |
| macOS arm64 sha256 | https://github.com/faberlang/releases/releases/download/faber-v1.5.0/faber-v1.5.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz.sha256 |
| Linux x64 tar.gz | https://github.com/faberlang/releases/releases/download/faber-v1.5.0/faber-v1.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz |
| Linux x64 sha256 | https://github.com/faberlang/releases/releases/download/faber-v1.5.0/faber-v1.5.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.sha256 |

Verify by comparing the first hash field in the `.sha256` file to the local archive hash; the checksum line may name the original build path. Extract `faber-v1.5.0-<target-triple>/faber`; place it on PATH; run `faber --version`.

Human install page: https://faberlang.dev/en-US/start/install.html

## CLI workflow

```bash
faber check <package>
faber build <package> -t rust
faber run <package>
faber test <package>
faber format <package>
faber explain <DIAG_CODE>
```

Default package product path often uses Rust → native via Cargo (one measured
HIR projection). Generated Rust uses faber-runtime types where required.
Support is stated target by target — see /en-US/toolchain/target-matrix.html.

## GPU device execution

Faber runs device programs on real GPUs. A package carries a device program
when its source declares an `@ nucleum` compute kernel and its manifest
declares a `[device]` section; the packaged image embeds Metal MSL and CUDA
PTX artifacts, each with a provenance hash.

```bash
faber run --backend metal <package>   # Apple Metal
faber run --backend cuda  <package>   # NVIDIA CUDA (NVVM → PTX)
faber run --backend auto  <package>   # resolve: exactly one admitted backend
```

Backend selection is explicit and fail-closed: a requested backend does not
silently fall back to CPU, it exits with a stable code.

Capability ladder — state these accurately, do not round up:

- Shipped: reader-localized source, diagnostics, formatting.
- Proven now: bounded dual-backend device training on Metal and CUDA —
  device-resident steps, gradient-slot → buffer mapping, end-of-run readback,
  numeric comparison against a pinned CPU oracle on an accepted MLP path.
  This is a real-device proof, not a general training framework and not a
  broad hardware-coverage claim.
- Building next: Faber-owned GPU inference behind a pinned model contract and
  correctness oracle. The CPU oracle track is real; end-to-end **device**
  inference is NOT shipped.
- Frontier: multi-device execution, virtual GPUs, sharding, and distributed
  training or serving are direction, not current runtime capabilities.

The corpus target matrix does not score `metal-text` / `wgsl-text`, and has no
`cuda` column. Those emitters lower a device-safe kernel subset only, so a
whole-language percentage does not apply to them. Do not infer weak GPU
support from their absence — read
/en-US/toolchain/target-matrix.html#device-kernel-support instead.

Pages: /en-US/toolchain/cli.html#device-execution ·
/en-US/toolchain/compiling.html · /en-US/toolchain/target-matrix.html

## Examples repository layout

https://github.com/faberlang/examples

```text
examples/
  corpus/          keyword / construct programs
  ai-workbench/    multi-command AI CLI application
  vivilite/        local mailspace / agent coordination CLI
  coreutils/       application campaign
  gpu-workload/    GPU systems rungs
  training/        device training fixtures (device-summa, mlp dual-backend oracle)
  automation/      automation sketches
  reader-locale/   locale demos
  scripta/         scripting demos
  script-kernel/   kernel-facing demos
  cista-lab/       package-store lab
```

Norma exempla (stdlib tours) live under the norma repo when present:
https://github.com/faberlang/norma

## Recommended agent procedure for a new package

1. Install `faber` 1.5.0 from releases; verify with `faber --version`.
2. Read language skill + one syntax page for constructs you will use.
3. Scaffold `faber.toml` + `src/main.fab` (or copy structure from vivilite / ai-workbench).
4. Loop: edit → `faber check` → fix diagnostics (`faber explain CODE`) → `faber test`.
5. Prefer patterns from examples over inventing new package layouts.
6. Do not invent `//` comments or C-like type-after-name declarations.

## Ecosystem libraries

| Import family | Repo | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `norma:*` | faberlang/norma | Standard library |
| `triga:*` | faberlang/triga | Graphics / geometry |
| cista | faberlang/cista | Package store CLI/lib |
| faber-runtime | faberlang/faber-runtime | Generated Rust support types |

## What not to assume

- Do not assume a public Radix source checkout is available.
- Do not assume Windows prebuilts (check the release page for new targets).
- Do not treat HTML alone as the agent contract — prefer llms.txt + skills.
- Do not weaken package structure to "make something compile"; fix the source.
- Do not treat bare `/start/…` paths as canonical; use `/en-US/…`.
- Do not claim GPU inference or multi-device execution as shipped; bounded
  dual-backend training is the current proven device claim.
- Do not read the absence of `metal-text` / `wgsl-text` / `cuda` from the
  corpus matrix as weak GPU support; see the device kernel support summary.
